newsitem.title: UK: Britain dismayed at Chinese dissident's sentence.
newsitem.headline: Britain dismayed at Chinese dissident's sentence.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday expressed dismay at the 11-year prison sentence handed down by a Chinese court to dissident and former student leader Wang Dan.
"We are dismayed by the heavy sentence that has now been given to Mr Wang Dan. His is one of a number of human rights cases which we have raised with the Chinese," a Foreign Office spokesman said.
"We urge the Chinese to show clemency and allow Wang's early release," he said.
The Beijing Number One Intermediate People's Court delivered the sentence after finding Wang guilty of plotting to overthrow the government.

"We continue to be concerned about human rights in China and we have consistently urged the Chinese authorities to respect fundamental freedoms including the right to freedom of expression," the British spokesman said.
He said Britain would be considering with its EU partners what further action to take. Britain hands its biggest remaining colony, Hong Kong, over to Chinese sovereignty next June.
Wang, 27, was found guilty of conspiring to subvert the Chinese government, sentenced to 11 years in prison and deprived of his political rights for a further two years, the Xinhua news agency said.
He had faced a maximum penalty of death and a minimum 10-year sentence.
